He was probably born around 1845, and the census records of 1850 and 1860 place him as a young son in the household of Thomas Flynn in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. His 1908 death certificate, also in Schuylkill County, names Thomas Flynn as his father. The records disagree on where he was born: the census says Ireland, while the death certificate says Pennsylvania. There is also a real doubt about whether the 1850 boy is the same Patrick who died in 1908, because two Patrick Flynns of about the same age lived in the county that year. From 1860 until his death in 1908 there are no records found for him, which is a long silence; the 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses should show where he was during those decades, and the family may have moved or the records may not have been found yet.
The next step is to settle the birthplace disagreement and the identity question before going further.
